caption: System design starts with guarantees, not a shopping list of tools. Ask what users do, how much load to expect, and which failures are acceptable. #systemdesign #beyondlocalhost

scenes.title: Before you draw a single box…
scenes.narration: You are asked to design a chat app. Do you start with a database? First, ask what this system must guarantee. A good architecture starts with the problem.

scenes.title: Same product. Different system.
scenes.narration: A family chat and an emergency dispatch system both send messages. But a delayed family message and a delayed emergency alert have very different consequences.
scenes.note: The name of the product is not enough.

scenes.title: Ask what users actually do.
scenes.narration: Define the core user flow. A person sends a message. Another person receives it. Must users search history? Can they send while the receiver is offline?

scenes.title: Then ask how well it must work.
scenes.narration: Now define measurable constraints. How many active users? What delivery delay is acceptable? Can a confirmed message ever be lost? These answers drive capacity and durability choices.

scenes.title: Ask what happens during failure.
scenes.narration: If a region disconnects, should the system accept messages with delayed delivery? Or refuse until it can guarantee the result? Decide what the user sees before choosing components.
scenes.note: A failure policy is a product decision.

scenes.title: A defensible design starts here.
scenes.narration: Remember three questions. What must users do? How much load must we serve? What must remain true when something fails? Next, turn those assumptions into a traffic estimate.
